A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAPS research. Their full main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, plots and qualitative examples, support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched despite substantial renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet-256 and LAFAN, hyperparameter ablations, generated samples and simulated robot-control demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds non-autoregressive comparisons, bottleneck-scaling experiments, latent-code utilization analyses and computational measurements.

M1.justification: v2 introduces DAPS-NA, replacing autoregressive latent generation with a decoder-only transformer that produces all logits in one forward pass. This is a concrete architectural adaptation, while the central nonparametric target, weighted-likelihood encoder objective, decoder objective and ESS adaptation remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet-256 and retargeted LAFAN motions, including latent-space image generation and goal-conditioned robot control. The added capacity sweeps, architecture variants and utilization measurements concern retained data and tasks rather than new coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add Gumbel-NA and GRMCK-NA comparisons alongside the retained autoregressive methods, FSQ, VQ-VAE and PPO. Gumbel-NA also supplies an ImageNet reconstruction comparator where autoregressive Gumbel remains excluded. These additions substantially broaden the comparison beyond autoregressive gradient estimators.

E3.justification: v2 adds PSNR and SSIM evaluation, bottleneck-size sweeps and resource profiling, and enlarges VQ networks to better match parameter budgets. Reported MNIST decoder and beta/ESS settings change. LAFAN inputs change from 127 to 121 features in Section 4 and Appendix J.1, although Appendix J retains 127. These are reported setting revisions, not evidence of performance gains under unchanged conditions.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained beta/ESS and baseline-sample ablations, v2 tests autoregressive versus non-autoregressive architectures, reconstruction scaling with bottleneck capacity, empirical vocabulary utilization, and memory/speed tradeoffs. Appendices F–H provide substantial new evidence about capacity sensitivity, representation behavior and computational scalability.

E5.justification: Appendix F specifies five seeds for the new tiny, small and medium bottleneck experiments and reuse of ten-seed main experiments for large bottlenecks. Main benchmark repetition counts remain ten seeds, or five for ImageNet, and summary curves retain the mean plus/minus one standard error convention. There is no stated increase in existing benchmark repetitions.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive non-autoregressive, PSNR/SSIM, scaling, utilization and computational results. Existing entries also change: MNIST DAPS beta=0.01 ELBO changes from -49.49 to -46.54, and ImageNet VQ-VAE FID from 76.78 to 65.01, alongside revised settings. These are replaced results rather than established same-setting improvements. DAPS ImageNet FID remains 48.65; newly evaluated Gumbel-NA obtains 51.66.

T1.justification: The constrained optimum and ESS/Renyi-2 theoretical development are retained. Appendix A's derivation, lemma, corollary and proofs are unchanged apart from notation. Section 3 expands the return/baseline explanation and makes the Monte Carlo expression more explicit, without a substantive new derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the specific claim of a 20% ImageNet FID improvement. The introduction more prominently highlights expressive robot control, whose demonstration already existed in v1. The central contributions—discrete VAE training through policy search without reparameterization and strong reconstruction performance—remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of architecture, entropy and computational tradeoffs. It attributes Gumbel-NA's advantage over Gumbel to autoregressive gradient-estimation difficulty and connects broad code utilization to entropy regularization. Appendix H acknowledges computational costs and confines efficiency advantages to appropriate comparators. Appendix F qualifies scaling findings by noting different optimization objectives and no advantage at the tiny CIFAR bottleneck.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer, a full MNIST architecture configuration, explicit GR-MCK sampling counts, method- and beta-specific hyperparameter Tables 3–6, and GPU, memory and throughput details in Appendix H. However, v1's explicit FSQ level lists and online Welford-normalization statement are omitted. Documentation therefore expands substantially but loses some reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Higgins et al. on beta-VAE, Greensmith et al. on variance reduction, and Ziebart on maximum causal entropy, while removing Kober et al. The exposition more explicitly positions DAPS within episode-based policy search. Its principal relationship to REPS, V-MPO, SPU and LBPS remains.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten around episode-based policy search and a separate variance-reduction explanation, and Algorithm 1 is reorganized into weight-computation and update procedures. The results narrative is reworked around separate beta settings, ablations move into the experiments section, and model-specific hyperparameters are integrated into dataset architecture appendices. These changes extend beyond inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: The original combined results table becomes two reorganized tables, and the hyperparameter summary figure becomes Tables 3–6. v2 adds utilization heatmaps, capacity-scaling plots and computational bar charts, redraws metric summaries, and revises Figure 1. Existing reconstruction and robotics images are retained and relocated rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the support for its central performance and scalability claims through non-autoregressive comparators, parameter-budget controls, capacity sweeps and direct computational measurements. The new ImageNet Gumbel-NA result, FID 51.66 against DAPS's 48.65, exposes a closer competitor, while the abstract drops its 20% headline claim and the discussion better qualifies efficiency. Expanded implementation documentation also helps reproducibility. Missing FSQ settings and inconsistent LAFAN feature counts are drawbacks, but they do not outweigh the substantial gains in comparison quality, validation and interpretation.
